items.reason: The rollup CLI keeps the outputs tree in undocumented /tmp/merkle.dat, ignores load/save errors and rewrites non-atomically; a lost or short file silently resets the tree so the next accept writes a root omitting earlier outputs. Demonstrated with the io-mock driver.

items.brief_for_prover: DEFECT: machine-guest-tools v0.18.1-test1 sys-utils/rollup/rollup.cpp class rollup: constructor cmt_rollup_load_merkle(&m_rollup, "/tmp/merkle.dat") and destructor cmt_rollup_save_merkle(...) both ignore their return values; libcmt merkle.c cmt_merkle_load copies into the live struct before checking the length; util.c cmt_util_write_whole_file truncates (fopen "wb") then writes. The save happens after the output yield. A missing/short file resets the tree (next notice gets index 0 again), and the next `rollup accept` writes a root omitting earlier outputs; the tool exits 0. TRIGGER: an application using the rollup CLI as documented whose /tmp loses or fails to write the file because of input-driven conditions: e.g. the app stores input data in /tmp/tmpfs until full before its first output, so the first save (file did not exist, nothing freed by truncation) fails silently; or the app clears /tmp scratch files; or the rollup process is killed/SIGPIPE after the yield. REQUIRED: section 2 correctly designed application: 'When it accepts, it leaves in the tx buffer the outputs Merkle root of every output it accepted'; section 3 Guest software Critical clause; R7 'The rx buffer, the tx buffer, and the yield interface'. TEST IDEA: machine from the guest-tools rootfs (bugs/harness valid-template style) with entrypoint: rollup accept; notice 0x01; accept; rm -f /tmp/merkle.dat (or fill /tmp before the first notice); notice 0x02; accept. Deliver inputs; assert the second accept's tx-buffer root equals the frontier root of both output hashes and the second notice index is 1. Exit 1 today. Document which input-driven trigger the test models, so review can judge 'documented use'. threat_model_gaps: Component table vs section 3: AUDIT.md assigns 'Referee verifier' to machine-solidity-step as a whole, while section 3 defines a referee verifier as one 'whose acceptance settles disputes' and support as 'copies of the verifiers whose acceptance settles nothing'. MetaStep.step in that library is never called by pinned Dave (R1-R11-1: Critical vs Medium).

Clock sizing in the referee model: unclear whether a deployed referee's clocks sized below the worst-case R12 cost count as a defect that 'only changes how long a claim may take to respond' (support, Medium) or as an A7 failure caused by the emulator's worst-case cost (Critical). Also, section 2 bounds a correctly designed application's mcycles only, not its uarch cycles per mcycle or its input count (R1-A7-1, R1-R12-1, R1-A7-2).

A5's 'No party can make it stop accepting them': unclear whether a privileged role the deployment configures (the rollups guardian, foreclosure) is such a party or a trusted part of the deployment (R1-A5-1).

Section 4 says 'the manual must state this requirement', which is a requirement on the manual. No section 8 case says whether violating it is Medium ('violates a rule or the manual') or Low (R1-R14-2).

O1/section 4: unclear whether a snapshot whose hashed contents meet every valid-template condition must stay adoptable when its cached hash-tree structure is malformed or missing, and whether a loud load error counts as 'crash the honest operator'. Non-hashed config.json fields such as hash_tree.phtc_size are neither 'cached hash-tree data' nor a valid-template condition (R1-O1-1, R1-O1-2).
R4 configuration clause: unclear whether it binds independently of the valid-template conditions, and whether 'register values' covers uarch RAM contents given in a configuration (R1-R4-1).

R13 'reproducibly buildable': unclear whether this requires pinned build inputs (toolchain versions, base-image digest) or only that today's rebuild matches. The High case's qualifier 'while what is deployed matches its audited source' is also ambiguous when the audited source cannot be built without a hand edit (R1-R1-1, R1-R13-1).

Output/yield exclusion: unclear whether it excuses a per-yield cost that is bounded but larger than needed, and whether it covers console characters, which are neither outputs nor yields (R1-R8-3, R1-R14-1).
